label: Bella Union
description: Stratton's sixth album is a hushed, meticulously fingerpicked set that pairs Nick Drake-indebted guitar work with chamber-folk strings. It's patient, literate songwriting built for close listening rather than singalongs.
lineage: Grew from Stratton's decade-plus run as a solo-guitar folk songwriter; sounds indebted to Nick Drake and John Fahey.

label: Bella Union
description: A widescreen, string-laden folk record pairing Stratton's intricate fingerpicked guitar with orchestral arrangements. The songs about change and loss unfold slowly, for listeners who like chamber folk.
lineage: Continues Stratton's Bella Union run of chamber-folk records that sound descended from Nick Drake and American Primitive guitar playing.

label: Bella Union
description: Stratton's eighth album continues his dusky, tasteful, string-accented fingerstyle songwriting. It is patient, literate folk built for close listening.
lineage: Eighth solo album in a run stretching back to his 2007 debut; sounds indebted to Nick Drake and American Primitive fingerstyle guitar.

label: Outside Music
description: Recorded at La Frette studios near Paris, Loyalty is warm, unhurried indie folk with Tamara Lindeman's plainspoken alto out front and light Americana touches (pedal steel, brushed drums).
lineage: Tamara Lindeman's long-running Toronto folk project, moving from 2000s singer-songwriter records toward the more expansive, band-driven indie folk of its 2020s run.
key_tracks: Way It Is, Way It Could Be

label: Outside Music
description: The self-titled fourth album is Lindeman's most purely indie-folk record, wistful full-band songs about love and self-doubt. Jangling guitars sit under close, conversational vocals.
lineage: Tamara Lindeman's long-running Toronto folk project, moving from 2000s singer-songwriter records toward the more expansive, band-driven indie folk of its 2020s run.

label: Fat Possum
description: A record that folds saxophone, flute and disco-adjacent rhythm into Lindeman's folk songwriting. Climate anxiety runs underneath as its emotional undertow.
lineage: Tamara Lindeman's long-running Toronto folk project, moving from 2000s singer-songwriter records toward the more expansive, band-driven indie folk of its 2020s run.

album: How Is It That I Should Look at the Stars
label: Next Door Records
description: Written alongside Ignorance but left spare and largely acoustic, this companion album is quieter and more intimate, letting Lindeman's voice and guitar carry most of the weight.
lineage: Tamara Lindeman's long-running Toronto folk project, moving from 2000s singer-songwriter records toward the more expansive, band-driven indie folk of its 2020s run.

label: Fat Possum
description: Humanhood leans further into improvisation and a loose full-band feel. It keeps Lindeman's core folk songwriting intact under the restless arrangements.
lineage: Tamara Lindeman's long-running Toronto folk project, moving from 2000s singer-songwriter records toward the more expansive, band-driven indie folk of its 2020s run.

label: Ba Da Bing!
description: Hollie Fullbrook's Tiny Ruins widens its hushed, literate folk with warmer full-band arrangements. Her soft, precise voice stays at the center, for fans of patient, wordy indie folk.
lineage: Grew from Fullbrook's solo Tiny Ruins recordings into a full band; sounds akin to Southern Hemisphere songwriters like Julia Jacklin.

label: Milk! Records
description: Tiny Ruins' fourth album is patient, pastoral folk-rock built around Hollie Fullbrook's plainspoken voice. The band plays with restraint, letting fingerpicked guitar and soft rhythm carry the songs.
lineage: Continues the Auckland band's decade-plus run of Flying Nun/Bella Union-adjacent indie folk.

label: Dear Life Records
description: Hill's debut sets intricate fingerpicking under a plainspoken, nature-fixated songwriting voice. It sounds indebted to Michael Hurley and Karen Dalton, for listeners who like patient solo-guitar folk.
lineage: Sounds rooted in the American Primitive fingerstyle tradition, opening onto her fuller-band later records.

label: Dear Life Records
description: A transitional second record that opens Hill's solo fingerstyle sound to a small circle of collaborators. The warm, unhurried arrangements stay close to her voice and guitar.
lineage: Follows Azalea, expanding her palette ahead of the full-band Hopeful Woman.

label: Dear Life Records
description: Hill's third LP is her most fleshed-out, twang-forward record yet, with pedal steel and flute threaded through full-band arrangements. Her fingerpicked guitar and plainspoken voice remain the anchor.
lineage: Continues Hill's fingerstyle-folk lineage into pedal-steel-laced country-folk.
key_tracks: Blue is the Color of My Sun

label: Thirty Tigers
description: Uwade Akhere's debut full-length showcases a studied, soaring voice. It moves through folk, soul and singer-songwriter modes with patient, warm arrangements.
lineage: Emerged after her lead vocal on the opening track of Fleet Foxes' Shore; sounds akin to Fleet Foxes-adjacent harmonic folk.

label: Self-released
description: A prolific Bandcamp DIY songwriter's lo-fi home recording, titled with a wry nod to AC/DC. It carries a loose, sci-fi-inflected sense of humor under its homemade folk.
lineage: Sounds akin to the sprawling, self-released Bandcamp DIY-folk underground, alongside acts like Sleeper's Bell and Hazel City.

label: Self-released
description: Quiet guitar-and-voice folk arrangements with occasional full-band lift. It is a modest, patient DIY record for listeners who like hushed home-grown songwriting.
lineage: Sounds akin to the current Bandcamp indie-folk underground alongside Hazel City.

album: Learning to Be a Cowboy on the Horse That Broke My Arm
label: Community Music
description: A six-track Bay Area folk EP with a wry, self-deprecating title track sequence, sparse acoustic arrangements built around plainspoken storytelling.
lineage: Bay Area indie-folk scene alongside Mae Powell and Abbey Blackwell.

label: Colemine Records
description: A jazz-inflected folk-rock record carried by Powell's standout voice and a warm band. Its immaculate instrumental textures suit listeners who like soul-tinged folk.
lineage: Sounds indebted to classic soul and jazz-folk singers as much as to indie folk.

label: Lame-O Records
description: A heart-wrenching record written for a friend, with Lily Seabird's voice swinging from a whisper to a shriek. Muscular, clanging guitars push the quiet songs into full-band rock.
lineage: Part of the Burlington, Vermont scene bridging indie folk and full-band rock.

label: Lame-O Records
description: Big-hearted, warm indie rock and folk about finding home and belonging amid chaos. It continues Seabird's mix of hushed verses and full-throated choruses.
lineage: Follow-up to Alas within the Burlington, VT indie-folk/rock scene.

label: Lame-O Records
description: Seabird's fourth LP balances explosive, searing electric guitar passages with quiet, dexterous lead-guitar moments and hushed verses, continuing her run of Lame-O Records albums about home and belonging.
lineage: Fourth album from the Vermont songwriter, continuing the Lame-O Records Burlington-scene run.

label: New West Records
description: Sunny War's breakout blends folk-punk fingerpicking with gospel, blues and roots textures. Songs about addiction and recovery ride a full-band Americana sound.
lineage: Grew from War's Venice Beach busking roots into a full-band Americana sound; its punk-inflected roots music sounds akin to Sadurn.

label: New West Records
description: A kinetic follow-up to Anarchist Gospel, moving from acoustic to electric guitar with guests Valerie June, Tre Burt and Steve Ignorant of Crass, exploring memory and haunted-house ghosts.
lineage: Continues War's New West run of roots-punk/gospel-blues records.

label: Secretly Canadian
description: Donnelly's debut pairs plainspoken, funny-sad lyrics, many of them pointed portraits of bad men, with light, jangly indie-folk arrangements. The songs are sharp and conversational, and the quiet backing leaves the wit and anger right at the front.
lineage: Grew out of Donnelly's 2017 Thrush Metal EP and the Perth DIY scene; part of the same wry Australian singer-songwriter lineage as Julia Jacklin.

label: Metropolitan Groove Merchants
description: Donnelly's second album keeps the wit of her debut while opening into fuller, more atmospheric arrangements. Her sharp, clear voice sits among piano and gentle band textures.
lineage: Follow-up to Beware of the Dogs, self-released after leaving Secretly Canadian.

label: Dot Dash Recordings
description: Donnelly's third and most introspective album pairs sparse, spacious production with conversational, incisive lyrics and timeless pop-folk melodies. It is a step back from Flood's fuller arrangements.
lineage: Third album, released via Dot Dash Recordings/Remote Control after two self-directed records.

label: ANTI-
description: Recorded with Mike Mogis in Omaha after signing to ANTI-, Dark Arc pairs dulcimer-and-mandolin folk instrumentation with denser production. The electric edge gives the stomping group vocals more push.
lineage: Zac Little's Columbus, OH string-band project, drawing on Appalachian instrumentation (balalaika, dulcimer, mandolin) filtered through indie folk-rock.

label: ANTI-
description: A pop-structured folk-rock record built on the band's trademark mix of banjo, dulcimer and balalaika. Synths and electric guitars push the songs outward.
lineage: Zac Little's Columbus, OH string-band project, drawing on Appalachian instrumentation (balalaika, dulcimer, mandolin) filtered through indie folk-rock.

label: ANTI-
description: An unexpected folk-rock record mixing Appalachian string-band instrumentation with contemporary electronic touches. Zac Little's high, urgent voice leads the layered arrangements.
lineage: Zac Little's Columbus, OH string-band project, drawing on Appalachian instrumentation (balalaika, dulcimer, mandolin) filtered through indie folk-rock.

label: Lame-O Records
description: Saintseneca's first album in seven years is full of heady surrealist lyrics. Rousing, off-kilter earworm hooks carry its string-band folk-rock.
lineage: Zac Little's Columbus, OH string-band project, drawing on Appalachian instrumentation (balalaika, dulcimer, mandolin) filtered through indie folk-rock.

label: Mare Records
description: Living Water is a spare folk record built on close-mic'd guitar and Lay's airy voice. It sounds indebted to Nick Drake and Vashti Bunyan.
lineage: Lay's second solo album, made while she played in the LA punk band Feels; sounds akin to the LA cosmic-folk revival around Ty Segall's circle.

label: Sub Pop
description: Lay's first album for Sub Pop, co-produced with Ty Segall. It dresses her fingerpicked folk with a wider array of instrumentation than her earlier records.
lineage: Marks Lay's move from Feels' punk records into a dedicated solo folk career.

label: All the Best
description: Lay's latest adds pedal steel, piano and synths to her folk core with a larger team of musicians than before. Her airy voice and fingerpicking stay at the center.
lineage: Follows Geist as Lay's most expansive solo record to date.

label: Verve Forecast Records
description: Goodman's second album sharpens her rural-Kentucky storytelling into a bleaker, more electric record about depression and rural isolation. The arrangements lean harder into fuzzy guitar than her debut without losing its plainspoken drawl. A more confident, harder-hitting follow-up.
lineage: Extends Old Time Feeling's western-Kentucky storytelling into darker territory; sounds close to Ian Noe and the post-Childers Kentucky scene.
key_tracks: If You Were Someone I Loved
borderline_note: Rock-leaning tracks could equally sit in C2; kept here for its folk/country storytelling core.

label: Slough Water Records
description: Goodman's third album turns toward the folk-magic and planting traditions of rural Kentucky for its imagery. It keeps the plainspoken, rootsy sound of her earlier records while widening its spiritual and agricultural language. A settled, personal record from one of the scene's most distinctive Kentucky voices.
lineage: Continues Goodman's western-Kentucky storytelling; its imagery draws on the region's folk traditions.

label: Free Dirt Records
description: Shame is iconoclastic bluegrass-rooted folk with pointed, feminist political songwriting. Baiman's fiddle playing anchors the lean arrangements.
lineage: Oak Park, Illinois-raised fiddler turned Nashville songwriter; sounds rooted in the politically engaged old-time and bluegrass-folk tradition.

label: Signature Sounds Recordings
description: An investigation of generational cycles and inherited pain. It is delivered through Baiman's old-time-inflected fiddle-and-banjo folk songwriting.
lineage: Solo record marking Baiman's move from Free Dirt to Signature Sounds.

label: Signature Sounds Recordings
description: Timeless, justice-minded folk tunes rooted in Baiman's old-time fiddle playing. It is for listeners who like protest songs in a warm Nashville string-band setting.
lineage: Continues Baiman's politically engaged Americana songwriting on Signature Sounds.

label: Full Time Hobby
description: Sam Swinson's band makes its debut with dark, twangy country-Americana about addiction and recovery. Sauntering guitars and a weary, close-up vocal give it a lived-in storytelling core.
lineage: Its dark, lived-in country-folk storytelling sounds akin to rural-leaning indie bands like Wednesday.
borderline_note: Country-rock band; flagged as a judgment call between C5 and C2's barroom-storyteller sound.

label: Orindal Records
description: A knotty, dense, patient listen that veers between mesmerizing folk, psych drone and glitchy ambient textures. It comes from the former Rodan bassist turned solo songwriter.
lineage: O'Neil's long solo run (Quarterstick, K Records, Kranky) traces from post-rock roots into hushed, experimental indie folk; now on the same Orindal roster as Wednesday.

album: To Enjoy Is the Only Thing
label: Partisan Records
description: Tori Zietsch's debut as Maple Glider, produced by Tom Iansek, draws on vignettes of her life and travel. The spare, intimate folk songs center her clear, hushed voice.
lineage: Launched Zietsch's solo folk career on Pieater/Partisan.

label: Partisan Records
description: Emotionally devastating songs about religion, bodily autonomy and trauma. It sits in the same territory as Julia Jacklin's Pre Pleasure, with spare arrangements around a close vocal.
lineage: Second album, continuing Maple Glider's confessional Australian indie-folk songwriting.

label: Western Vinyl
description: A quiet, falsetto-led folk record continuing Temple's Paul Simon- and Nick Drake-indebted songwriting. It stands apart from his Art Feynman and Here We Go Magic projects.
lineage: Longtime Secretly Canadian/Western Vinyl songwriter (Here We Go Magic, Art Feynman) returning to plain solo-folk songwriting.

label: Winspear
description: Lutalo Jones' debut album turns knotty indie rock and warm folk into a bigger, bolder coming-of-age record. It is fuller and more ambitious than the lo-fi Once Now, Then Again EP.
lineage: Vermont-based multi-hyphenate whose folk-rooted songwriting sounds akin to the Burlington DIY scene around Lily Seabird.

album: Every Time We Turn A Corner
label: Royal Mountain Records
description: Understated, catchy hushed-folk pop built on delicate rhythm-section grooves. George Harrison-style slide guitar is layered over plainspoken verses.
lineage: Signed to Royal Mountain Records; sounds akin to current hushed-folk-pop songwriters such as Ultra Lights and Proun.
key_tracks: Every Time We Turn A Corner

label: Self-released
description: Nicole Rodriguez's Pearla turns from the mysteries of the external world to the interior and relational. Sparse, acoustic arrangements frame intimate songs.
lineage: Sounds akin to hushed indie-folk songwriters such as Sadurn and Greg Mendez.

label: Northern Spy
description: A dreamworld folk-pop record mixing hushed vocals, vintage guitar tones and bossa nova influence. The arrangements feel like a neon-lit western dive bar at closing time.
lineage: Brooklyn songwriter whose Northern Spy records fold bossa nova and folk into a spectral sound akin to Timber Timbre.

label: Run For Cover Records
description: Genevieve DeGroot's full-band debut is spare, diary-like indie folk. It sounds indebted to Jason Molina, Gillian Welch and Elliott Smith.
lineage: Grew from DeGroot's lo-fi Philadelphia DIY recordings into a full band; part of the Philly indie-folk scene alongside Greg Mendez.

label: Self-released
description: A raspy-voiced, earthy folk record built on fingerstyle guitar. It is warm, patient music for listeners who like American Primitive playing with songs attached.
lineage: Fingerstyle folk that sounds rooted in the same Appalachian/American Primitive lineage as Jake Xerxes Fussell.

label: Grand Jury Music
description: Dan Álvarez de Toledo and Jordan Dunn-Pilz's debut LP runs on finish-each-other's-sentences vocal harmony. The songs dig into family history and young-adult self-reflection.
lineage: Duo songwriting that sounds indebted to Elliott Smith and Golden Daze.

label: Massif Records
description: Unfussy yet ornate indie folk-rock ranging from stripped melancholy to lush grooves. It suits listeners who like carefully arranged, low-key songwriting.
lineage: Sounds akin to the Brooklyn indie-folk/rock circle around Katy Kirby and Lindsay Reamer.

label: Fire Records
description: Allen's follow-up to Candlepower is timeless folk in a classic songwriting lineage. It is anchored by her mesmerizing, wide-ranging voice.
lineage: Los Angeles songwriter whose delicate, literary folk sounds akin to Weyes Blood and Cate Le Bon's circle.

label: Secretly Canadian
description: Lauren Spear's debut as Le Ren is ten hushed, plainspoken folk songs, with a guest turn from Tenci. The arrangements stay spare and the delivery direct, letting the songs sit close to the listener.
lineage: Montreal songwriter whose spare, direct folk songwriting fits the same lineage as Gillian Welch by way of Joni Mitchell.

label: Anxiety Blanket Records
description: Buoyant, bittersweet folk-rock built on acoustic guitars, piano and orchestral touches. It follows 2024's Apple Core with a warm, '70s-leaning sound.
lineage: Los Angeles songwriter whose sound draws on '70s soft rock and folk-rock.
